svg.title: Well-child visit for a 20-month-old.
svg.desc: A white pupillary reflex instead of the expected red reflex (leukocoria) is never a normal finding and requires urgent ophthalmology referral to rule out retinoblastoma. Femoral pulses weaker than the radial pulses suggest coarctation of the aorta, since all peripheral pulses should normally be comparably strong, and a new murmur that persists and does not change with position needs cardiology follow-up, unlike an innocent transient murmur from ductus closure heard in early infancy. Growth tracking along the curve, a closed and flat anterior fontanel at this age, brisk capillary refill, physiologic bowlegged stance in a toddler, and normal symmetric reflexes are all expected findings that do not need referral.
